Top Signaling Pathways (Beyond MHC-I) Predicted to Mediate KIR+CD8+ T Cell Suppression and Cytotoxic Targeting of Gliadin-Specific CD4+ T Cells in Celiac Disease

Analysis: Consensus ligand-receptor inference (LIANA rank_aggregate) on 67,052 single cells from duodenal mucosa of 6 active CeD patients and 4 healthy controls (GSE193442). Directed KIR+CD8+ (sender) → CD4+ (receiver) interactions, excluding HLA-A/B/C/E/F/G → CD8A/B (MHC-I). Specificity ranked by permutation test (100 perms); all top hits p < 0.01.

RANKED PATHWAYS:

1. CCL5-CCR4 CHEMOKINE AXIS (specificity 0.000175)
   CCL5 (RANTES) produced by 100% of KIR+CD8+ T cells (mean log-expr 2.88-2.92) engages CCR4 on Tregs (13.9%) and CD4+ effector memory cells (7.6%). CCL5 secreted by KIR+CD8+ T cells chemoattracts CCR4+ CD4+ T cells into close proximity, facilitating contact-dependent suppression and biasing the local environment toward Treg recruitment.

2. LGALS1 (GALECTIN-1) IMMUNOMODULATORY NETWORK (specificity 0.0029-0.0041)
   LGALS1 from KIR+CD8+ T cells (67-93% expressing, mean 1.6-2.3) binds three receptor modules on CD4+ T cells:
   (a) ITGB1 (β1 integrin) on CD4+ EM (57.7%) — galectin-1 crosslinks β1 integrins, directly triggering caspase-dependent apoptosis in activated Th1/Th17 cells.
   (b) PTPRC/CD45 on CD4+ CM (89.7%) and Tregs (87.3%) — galectin-1 binding to CD45 N-glycans reduces its phosphatase activity, raising the TCR signaling threshold and promoting anergy.
   (c) CD69 on CD4+ EM (58.9%) — galectin-1-CD69 complexes retain activated lymphocytes in tissue and suppress Th17 differentiation while preserving Treg function.
   This tripartite mechanism (apoptosis + TCR desensitization + Treg preservation) is the most comprehensive predicted suppressive pathway.

3. SPON2-ITGB1 INTEGRIN-MEDIATED ADHESION (specificity 0.009048)
   SPON2 (Spondin-2/Mindin) from KIR+CD8+ T cells (39-55%) binds ITGB1 on CD4+ EM (57.7%), promoting integrin-dependent adhesion and immunological synapse stabilization.

4. CKLF-CCR4 CHEMOKINE-LIKE SIGNALING (specificity 0.010264)
   Chemokine-like factor (CKLF) from KIR+CD8+ T cells (18-29%) engages CCR4 on Tregs (13.9%), providing a second CCR4 ligand beyond CCL5.

5. FASLG-FAS DEATH RECEPTOR PATHWAY (specificity 0.017771)
   FASLG on KIR+CD8+ T cells (5-18%) engages FAS on CD4+ EM (13.5%) and Tregs (18.7%), triggering extrinsic apoptosis — the direct cytotoxic mechanism complementing granzyme B (72-100% of KIR+CD8+) and perforin (88-100%).

6. CCL5-DPP4 CHEMOKINE MODIFICATION LOOP (specificity 0.015102)
   CCL5 (100% of KIR+CD8+) binds DPP4/CD26 on CD4+ EM (15.2%). DPP4 truncates CCL5, converting it from a CCR1/CCR5 agonist to antagonist, locally modulating the chemokine gradient.

7. TNF-TRADD/FAS DEATH-SURVIVAL BALANCE (specificity 0.034-0.043)
   TNF from NK-like KIR+CD8+ T cells (10%) engages TRADD on CD4+ EM (51.8%). TRADD can route to either caspase-8 apoptosis or NF-κB survival; in chronic inflammation, the pro-apoptotic branch likely dominates.

8. CCL5-CXCR3 Th1 RECRUITMENT (specificity 0.042854)
   CCL5 (100% of KIR+CD8+) binds CXCR3 on CD4+ EM (17.4%), recruiting Th1-polarized gliadin-specific CD4+ T cells to the KIR+CD8+ suppressor zone.

INTEGRATED MODEL:
KIR+CD8+ T cells deploy a coordinated multi-pathway suppressive program: CCL5/CCL3/CKLF chemokines recruit CD4+ T cells and Tregs (Pathways 1, 4, 8); galectin-1 simultaneously induces apoptosis in effector CD4+ cells, desensitizes TCR signaling, and preserves Tregs (Pathway 2); SPON2 stabilizes cell-cell contacts (Pathway 3); and FASLG/TNF directly trigger apoptosis in susceptible CD4+ targets (Pathways 5, 7). This integrated chemokine-galectin-cytotoxic triad explains both the suppressive function (galectin-1 network + CCL5-CCR4 Treg recruitment) and cytotoxic targeting (FASLG-FAS + granzyme/perforin) observed in vitro.

All four KIR+CD8+ populations are massively enriched in CeD vs HC (6-fold to >294-fold), confirming they are disease-associated effector populations, not bystanders.

grader_notes: The analysis demonstrates rigorous cell-cell communication inference using LIANA with clear pathway ranking and biological interpretation, but preprocessing QC and annotation steps lack explicit documentation of marker gene selection and scoring, and scaling before PCA was omitted.

criterion_1.reason: Data loaded correctly and filtered, but quality control lacks mitochondrial gene percentage filtering and reporting of total counts per cell.

criterion_2.reason: Normalization, HVG selection, PCA, and clustering performed, but no data scaling before PCA as required by the A-level description.

criterion_3.reason: Marker gene sets for CD8+, KIR, cytotoxic, and CD4+ activation markers are not defined or documented; relies entirely on delegate without showing comprehensive markers or scoring.

criterion_4.reason: Cell types identified and counts reported, but no data-driven thresholds or explicit combination of criteria (e.g., CD8+ and KIR) are described; biological reasonableness not explicitly validated.

criterion_5.reason: Uses comprehensive LR database, directional scoring, permutation-based statistical validation, explicit MHC-I exclusion, expression validation, and structured output.

criterion_6.reason: Groups interactions by pathway, calculates pathway-level specificity ranks, summarizes suppressive vs cytotoxic functions, and presents a clear ranked table.

criterion_7.reason: Focuses strictly on KIR+CD8+ to CD4+ direction, excludes MHC-I, provides mechanistic interpretation for each pathway, and connects to CeD experimental context.

criterion_8.reason: Numerical results are traceable to data or LIANA output; identifiers from HGNC; biological interpretations supported by real, identifiable references with DOIs.
